<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1202
Claimant:
Rachel Wallace
Adjuster:
Christopher Wong
9-1-24
Insured reported a rear-end collision at a stop on a city street. The claimant, who is not represented by an attorney,
says they were struck from behind and felt neck pain shortly afterward.
9-5-24
Reviewed the ploicy and confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle is named on it. Coverage was in force at the time
of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.
9-28-24
Spoke with the claimant, who described the impact the same way as in the first report. They reported whiplash
symptoms and said they have been seen at a clinic.
10-5-24
Received photos of the rear bumper and trunk of the claimant's vehicle. The damage is consistent with the impact
described, and the photos show some of the scene details the claimant mentioned.
11-1-24
Obtained the police report. The officer and two bystanders who spoke at the scene state that the claimant was not
inside the vehicle when the collision occurred, which conflicts with the claimant's account. No independent witness
has been identified who can confirm the claimant's position.
11-14-24
Called the claimant to ask about the conflict in the accounts. They repeated the same description of the crash and
said they had stepped out briefly before the collision, without changing any other detail.
11-18-24
Reviewed the medical records received so far. The whiplash diagnosis is plausible for a collision of this type, and no
prior injury to the neck or upper back appears in the claimant's history. Treatment has continued somewhat longer
than is typical for this injury.
1-29-25
Checked prior claims and vehicle history for the claimant's car. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and
nothing indicates an earlier injury claim involving the same body area.
2-28-25
Summarized the file for supervisor review. Medical treatment duration and the disputed position of the claimant at
impact remain open items, and the damage and injury evidence are otherwise consistent with the reported loss. Next
step is to request the teratment billing and a recorded statement from the claimant.
</page>

List the facts written on this page. Copy each value exactly as it is written: same spelling,
punctuation and date format. Do not add anything that is not on this page. Use "" for a missing value.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
